full_judgment:
5. Dr. M. Zahir, learned Counsel, appearing for the impugned judgment and order dated 12.12.2000 of the High Court Division is illegal inasmuch as the impugned judgment and order has been passed in violation of the provisions of Rules 5 and 6 of Order XXXVIII of the Code of Civil Procedure; that the appellant being the consignee of the buses is the legal owner of the buses and unless and until the shipping documents are retired by the respondent Nos.2 and 3 upon payment of money, the legal title to the buses shall remain with the appellant and since there is no claim against the appellant, its property cannot be attached on the application of third party; that the judgment and order dated 12.12.2000 passed by the High Court Division is illegal inasmuch as by the impugned judgment and order the High Court Division has attached the property of a third party against which the respondent No.1 as plaintiff has no claim; that pursuant to the provisions of Rule 5 order XXXVIII of the Code of Civil Procedure the property of the defendant can only be attached as security to satisfy the decree which may be passed against such defendant; that the judgment and order dated 12.12.2000 of the High Court Division is illegal inasmuch as the impugned judgment and order is seriously prejudicial to the appellant and the right of the appellant to recover its dues has been seriously affected by the impugned judgment and order. 

 6. Mr. T. H. Khan, learned Counsel, appearing for the respondent No. I submitted that it was a prima-facie case that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who imported the two buses in question by opening Letter of Credit through appellant Bank but it is the said defendants who in fact were the owners of the two buses and they advertised in the Daily Janakantha to sell those as noticed by the High Court Division, so it rightly disposed of the Rule with direction as given in the impugned judgment to see that in the event the plaintiff is decreed the same is executed as except the two buses sought to be attached the defendants have no other properties; that the plaintiff bank had the other legal remedies to recover the loan amount allegedly given to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 against the letter of credit for importing the two buses in question and other charges which the bank might have incurred in releasing the buses and in fact, it did not take any step when advertisement was made for selling the said two buses; that the High Court Division did not at all violate the provisions of Rules 5 and 6 of the order 38 of the Code of Civil Procedure in passing the impugned judgment and order as contended by the appellant. The learned Counsel further submitted that the appellant did not at all comply with the direction given by the High Court Division at the time of granting leave and the suit is decreed. The plaintiff shall not be in a position to execute the decree and as such, in order to do complete justice the appellant may he instructed to give proper security so that: the suit if decreed may be executed. 

 7. It appears that the High Court Division disposed the matter directing appellant, Dhaka Bank Ltd. to take immediate steps for release of two Double Decker Buses imported under Letter of Credit No.2031299231 and Bill of Lading NYKS00437056-7 on payment of all duties, taxes and charges and take them in its own custody. Then the Bank will sell the buses at the market price in public sale after giving at least seven days notice by publishing sale advertisement in two well circulated national dailies, subject to approval and overall supervision of the trial Court. Out of the sale proceeds, Tk. 43 lass must be deposited by Dhaka Bank in a fixed deposit at usual rate of interest to the credit of the trial Court and the receipt of the fixed deposit account must be placed in the custody of the Court. The fixed deposit will remain in the custody of the Court as security against the decree that may be passed till final decision of the suit and will, accordingly, be disposed of by the Court on the basis of its decision. Rest of the sale proceeds would be adjusted by Dhaka Bank against its own dues. 

 8. In view of the order of the High Court Division directing the appellant to take immediate steps for release of the Double Decker Buses imported under Letter of Credit No. 2031299231 and Bill of Lading NYKS00437056-7 on payment of all duties, taxes and charges and take them in its own custody for direction to sell the buses at market price in public sale after giving at least seven days notice by publishing sale advertisement in well circulated national dailies under the supervision of the trial Court. Accordingly the buses are sold in public sale and the same were sold at the highest bid and naturally after the sale the purchase sale proved was not enough and there was no enough money for deposit of TK. 43 lacs in the fixed deposit at usual rate of interest to the credit of the trial Court. After the order regarding the said deposit of TK. 43 lacs becomes impossible and no amount could he deposited to maintain as security against the decree passed on final disposal of the suit. 

 10. Accordingly, the order dated 12.12.2000 passed by the High Court Division is modified to the extent deleting the word "Out of the sale proceeds TK. 43 lees must be deposited by Dhaka Bank in a fixed deposit at usual rate of interest of the trial Court and the receipt of the fixed deposit account must be place in the custody of the Court. The fixed deposit will remain in the custody of the Court as security against the decree that may be passed till final decision of the suit."
